title: Spanish office cipher of 1592-93: Miranda to Feria, Sessa to Ibarra and to Philip II (BnF fr. 3983 nos. 45, 79; fr. 3984 no. 47; catalogue 19)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's Spanish page fetched as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: his key tables are images, and two of them cover exactly the folios this entry cites.

The catalogue's piece numbers resolved to folios through the BnF depouillement, and the folio-to-canvas map for fr. 3983 and fr. 3984 built by reading folio numbers off top strips and interpolating; all four leaves located.

Tomokiyo's Spanish Cipher (1592-93) transcribed to key92.tsv and applied to nos. 45 and 79: Spanish comes out (supongo que hava de ser, siendo confidente, a costa de la bolsa, a los sucesores, conviene), but with holes wherever the nomenclator is used.
No. 68's figures run far higher and the leaf carries three-letter word groups, so it is the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, as Tomokiyo's citation of f. 145 says, not the cipher of the other three.

The entry's own verify step followed: DECODE returns two records for these correspondents and both are keys, not letters, pointing into BnF fr. 3995. Folio 97 is the office's own key, complete with the nomenclature Tomokiyo lacks; key92.tsv extended to 133 entries.

The contemporary interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked against the key's own output on a third letter: del Passado con, por via de mar, difiriendo de dia en dia - agreement wherever both survive, and the bar, umlaut and trailing dot settled.
All four leaves read line by line from deskewed strips: 15 of 17 lines on no. 45, 14 of 16 on no. 79, the glossed lines on no. 47, and the opening of no. 68 with keyM.tsv.
The obvious candidate for the missing Feria-Mansfeld nomenclature, fr. 3995 f. 101, fetched and excluded: it is an Italian nomenclature belonging to another correspondence.

Novelty re-examined. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. 'Never applied' replaced by 'no published reading'.
A note from satorunet (3 Oct) said the nomenclature on fr. 3995 f. 97 has over 100 word entries against the 52 word entries in key92.tsv, and that the Parme-Roy endorsement is on f. 97v, not f. 98.

f. 97 (canvas 188) and canvases 189-190 read again from the Gallica images: the endorsement is on f. 97v and says the key serves for Sessa and Ibarra; f. 98 is a French key. 61 word entries added to key92.tsv (8 numeric ones, whose number is also a syllable, kept as comments), aviso revised for causa, the rule sheet read.

Unresolved groups of nos. 45, 79, 47 rerun with the full nomenclature: 13 resolved (50T = Su Magestad, 61T = tiempo, tim = intencion, nur = ninguna, pol = duque, hus = principe, cos = personas, vur = otro), Vor corrected to opinion, and the gloss 'en particular' on no. 47 confirms zir = particular.

The 0.70 fraction_read was checked: it counted every group not marked '·' as read, so syllables that make no Spanish word counted, and it under-counted the leaves (no. 79 has 22 cipher lines, not 14; no. 47 has 21, of which 13 were read). It was not a measure of sense.

Every cipher line of nos. 45, 79 and 47 re-transcribed from 3200-3600 px Gallica crops, including the 8 untranscribed lines of no. 79 (ll. 15-22) and 8 of no. 47 (ll. 14-21); each line scored for sense in sense.tsv (measure_sense.py).

f. 97 sheet re-checked for open groups: three-dot 94 and 95 = de; three-dot 49 = Su Santidad; three-dot 88 = V.M.; three-dot 5, 8, 9, 0, 25 = nulls; ʃo = assi (not aunque, which is ʒo). These resolve groups on all three leaves (confidente de S.M., a costa de la bolsa de S.M., mostrarla a Su Santidad, assi fuesse, assi devia).

Context readings forced in several places: 9 = y (adonde, omitido y assi), xor = para (variant of xur, three occurrences), pal = duque (variant of pol; duque de Feria, duque de Mantua), 86 = vo, 'de por tes' = Desportes, 67 90 62 = Pisani. Still open in the three letters: Val, ral, ʃep, ner, ʒe, pir, mil, is, xom, mal, rili, mos, ʃer, hir, hum, us, ho, yos, ∂ir, lir, xox, ru, not on the f. 97 sheet.
no. 68 scored for sense: 224/598. The new value belongs to the Mansfeld cipher, so the doubtful groups of nos. 45/79/47 (office key) gained nothing.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 68 (Ibarra, Paris, 10 Jul 1593), in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, moved to ibarra1593 with its files (ct68.txt, keyM.tsv, dec68.py, anneal68.py, fill68.py, reading68.md; its sense.tsv rows to sense68.tsv). measure_sense.py rerun on nos. 45/79/47: 1212/1310 = 0.925.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's cryptiana key image of the Spanish Cipher 1592-93 cites these folios (fr. 3983 ff. 98, 162), and the office's own key at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 (DECODE R4076-R4077, returned by a search for these correspondents) supplied the nomenclator; the interlinear gloss on no. 47 checked it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: sense.tsv / measure_sense.py (5 Oct 2026, rerun 14 Oct 2026 without no. 68): tokens read only where they form Spanish sense; doubtful readings and code groups without a value unread. no. 45 230/254 (0.906), no. 79 504/546 (0.923), no. 47 478/510 (0.937). Overall 1212/1310 = 0.925.
outcome.notes: Three letters read to about 92% of their groups on the office key (fr. 3995 f. 97), checked against the contemporary decipherment on no. 47. codes_open counts the 22 open groups of the three letters. No. 68, in the Feria-Mansfeld cipher, was split off to ibarra1593 on 14 Oct 2026 (the pooled 0.753 included it).

gaps.item: nos. 45, 79, 47: 22 code groups not on the f. 97 sheet (Val, ral, ʃep, ner, ʒe, pir, mil, is, xom, mal, rili, mos, ʃer, hir, hum, us, ho, yos, ∂ir, lir, xox, ru)
gaps.detail: the f. 97 sheet re-read 5 Oct for them; each occurs once or twice, too few for a context solution except where noted

gaps.item: nos. 45, 79, 47: about 75 syllable groups whose reading is doubtful (writer's slips, ambiguous hooks)

credits.note: PR #8: found the office's own key (BnF fr. 3995 f. 97) and read the three office-cipher letters in part; page byline
satorunet's note that the f. 97v endorsement labels the f. 97 key, and his count of the nomenclature, prompted the re-reading of the key sheet
key image for the Spanish Cipher 1592-93 (cryptiana spanish3.htm, phelippes2.png)
the office's own key at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 (DECODE R4076-R4077) and the interlinear gloss on no. 47

prior.where: Key published by Tomokiyo as an image on cryptiana (spanish3.htm), reconstructed from other letters with no published reading of these three; the office's own key survives at BnF fr. 3995 f. 97 and is catalogued on DECODE as records 4076-4077; a contemporary decipherer glossed part of no. 47. No published reading of any of the three letters.

human: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.
